transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-18
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Tom Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Acme Eng Mgr), Alex Gomez (Acme CTO), Samir Khan (Backend), Lena Ortiz (SRE)

Summary: quick SDK walk, auth options, env setup, demo of streaming and embeddings, discuss pilot and security.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood inference, this is tom our se, quick agenda - sdk quickstarts in python and typescript, auth patterns, console + optimize touchpoints, then tom will demo streaming and embeddings and we can talk pilot.
[00:14] Priya Patel: thanks maya, excited - we've been evaluating a few options, primary goals are low latency for chat features and reasonable cost at scale, plus must meet our security controls.
[00:27] Tom Alvarez: great, quick clarifying q: are you planning hosted api first or do you expect private/vpc on day one?
[00:34] Alex Gomez: ideally hosted to move fast, but security wants vpc option and kms for keys later. if pilot looks good we'll consider dedicated.
[00:45] Maya Chen: totally. for the sdk we have both python and typescript quickstarts - you can get started with an api key for quick dev, or we support service accounts and mTLS for private deployments. we'll share snippets after the call.
[00:57] Samir Khan: what's the auth flow for service accounts? do we exchange a short-lived token?
[01:04] Tom Alvarez: good q - for hosted we issue api keys with RBAC. for dedicated/private you can provision service accounts via the console which mint short-lived tokens tied to your KMS/HSM. we also support SSO for console access (saml/okta).
[01:20] Priya Patel: and env setup - how do devs set keys locally without committing them?
[01:25] Maya Chen: recommended pattern: set REDWOOD_API_KEY in environment, use .env for local dev and gitignore. for service accounts we recommend storing creds in a secrets manager and mounting into CI. we'll include a sample .env and github actions snippet.
[01:40] Alex Gomez: can you show the python quickstart real quick?
[01:44] Tom Alvarez: sure - i'll share my screen and walk through a tiny snippet. (screen share stutter) ok, python install pip install redwood-inference-sdk, then from redwood import Client; client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')); resp = client.generate(model='rw-1.3b', prompt='hello'); print(resp.text)
[02:10] Priya Patel: simple enough. streaming support? we need streaming to feed tokens to the frontend.
[02:16] Tom Alvarez: yes, streaming is supported in both python and ts. example in python: for chunk in client.stream_generate(...): render(chunk.text) - in ts you get an event emitter or async iterator. note: streaming can increase connections; we recommend a small connection pool at the proxy.
[02:33] Samir Khan: what about embeddings? we plan to embed product descriptions for search rerank.
[02:38] Tom Alvarez: embeddings are a separate endpoint, same client: client.embeddings.create(model='rw-emb-v1', input=['...']); we return numpy-friendly arrays in python or float32 arrays in ts. optimize integrates here - Redwood Optimize can analyze your embedding traffic and suggest quantization or caching.
[02:55] Priya Patel: can optimize help reduce cost without hurting rerank quality?
[02:59] Maya Chen: yes, Optimize will run sample evaluations on your prompt set, recommend model variants and quantization profiles. it also surfaces quality regressions over time.
[03:09] Lena Ortiz: on compliance - we need audit logs and retention controls, and encryption at rest with customer-managed keys.
[03:16] Maya Chen: we support audit logs, long retention as an add-on, and CMK via KMS/HSM for private/dedicated. we'll include SOC 2 and iso docs, and a KMS integration note.
[03:29] Alex Gomez: latency numbers - what should we expect for a 1k token generation on hosted rw-1.3b?
[03:34] Tom Alvarez: typical p95 is ~220-350ms per 512 tokens on optimized runtimes, but it varies with sequence length and batch behavior. for heavier workloads we recommend dedicated pools with tuned batch sizes. we'll propose a small benchmark run as a pilot.
[03:52] Priya Patel: traffic patterns - we have spiky QPS during promos, can we autoscale?
[03:58] Maya Chen: Dedicated supports autoscaling and burst capacity; hosted can burst across capacity tiers but dedicated gives more predictability and isolation. caching and prefix KV cache help for repeated prompts.
[04:10] Samir Khan: any gotchas in the sdk integration - e.g., long-running streams, reconnects?
[04:15] Tom Alvarez: handle reconnects idempotently; we expose delta tokens so you can resume cleanly. we also return request ids for tracing into the console.
[04:26] Priya Patel: demo request - can you show quickly the console mapping? where do we see usage and token breakdown?
[04:31] Maya Chen: yep. (quick console demo) per-route usage, token breakdown, error traces, model rollout controls. you can pin versions and set canary rules. we'll share a recording of the console tour.
[04:47] Alex Gomez: cost question - how do you recommend we structure dev vs prod keys to avoid accidental charges?
[04:52] Maya Chen: separate projects with quota, and dev keys on lower-cost model variants; console has quota and rate-limit per key. we can help set that up in pilot.
[05:03] Priya Patel: perfect. next steps?
[05:07] Maya Chen: action items: i'll send quickstart snippets and security docs; tom will prepare pilot capacity config and cost estimate; we ask acme to send sample prompts + traffic shape. then schedule follow-up next week.
[05:23] (crosstalk)
[05:30] Priya Patel: one thing - our SRE wants to know if we can route traffic regionally for data residency.
[05:36] Tom Alvarez: yes, smart routing supports region pinning and fallbacks; private deployment can be fully on-prem if required. we'll include region and routing notes.
[05:47] Maya Chen: ok wrapping up - i'll share the docs, repo link, and a short video. thanks everyone.
[05:54] Alex Gomez: thanks, appreciate it.
